blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Tagalog politeness markers, particularly opo and po, have increasingly found their way into everyday Cebuano conversations, as reflected in sample utterances such as “Opo, sir,” “Salamat po,” and even “Asa diay ka po?” The first two expressions sound unmistakably Tagalog, and their use is so natural, it often occurs without notice.
